question.knowledge_point: Computing a Probability on an Unbounded Interval
question.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14069722/assets/f25b8fea7403579d1ee40cc00b9447e3362dc28c2e9d41f762f51df5e11daaf8.png)

For a random variable $Z∼N(0,1),$ we have the following symmetry property for $a>0:$

$$
P(Z>a)=P(Z<-a)=Φ(-a)
$$

We're given that $Z∼N(0,1),$ and we wish to compute $P(Z>2.31).$ The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14069722/assets/a3e01ca4fd737cea9afe95374a17c0428f83a6717d98a7557222a856aa2d0c02.png)

By symmetry, this equals the area corresponding to the probability $P(Z<-2.31).$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14069722/assets/ce206061194e357b9cd75f9b260e4035a8600726a17cc0ee04ab39219bd45e94.png)

Therefore,

$$
P(Z>2.31)=P(Z<-2.31)=Φ(-2.31)=0.0104.
$$
